content:
Apple is set to hold a major launch event in September, where it will unveil three new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Below is a roundup of everything we know so far.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed the well-received iPhone 17 Pro series.

Rumoured new features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, delivering improved performance and energy efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, with the main lens featuring a variable aperture
  • Dynamic Island shrunk by 35%, giving the design a more modern look
  • Several new colour options, with a bold burgundy standing out as the most eye-catching
  • The best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing significant gains
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 modem chip
  • New satellite connectivity features, including 5G satellite links

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to see another price hike. Market estimates put the starting price at around US$1,399, though I believe the actual price will be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to be the name of Apple's first foldable phone, with an expected price tag north of US$2,000, carving out a brand-new premium category.

Its foldable form factor will inevitably make the iPhone Ultra the most groundbreaking model Apple has ever released. The device will adopt a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of around 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, delivering an experience akin to an iPad mini.

The build materials are expected to match those of the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame and a streamlined design.

The iPhone Ultra will come equipped with two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide), as well as two front-facing cameras serving the inner and outer displays. Authentication will switch from Face ID to Touch ID.

The software experience will be the device's biggest highlight, with the accompanying iOS 27 supporting side-by-side multitasking and automatically adapting layouts for landscape orientation to make the most of the new form factor.

Performance is expected to match that of the iPhone 18 Pro, with the same A20 Pro chip, a vapour chamber cooling system, and the C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, the September event should also see the launch of a new entry-level iPhone 18 and a successor to the iPhone Air.

However, this year Apple is reportedly adjusting its autumn product lineup, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this is purely a strategic decision or forced by current memory supply constraints. Whatever the reason, the absence of more affordable models means this autumn's new iPhone lineup will be entirely focused on the high end.

Are you planning to upgrade your iPhone this autumn? Which model has caught your eye? Feel free to share in the comments.
